summary: Recent changes to the connection transport in Firefox focus on improving the handling of WebRTC, the technology behind video calls. By moving `RTCIceCandidate`, a crucial component used for establishing web connections, out of the JavaScript implementation, the browser can now manage these connection attempts more efficiently. Additionally, implementing type and constant correctness fixes in the nICEr library enhances the reliability and performance of ICE (Interactive Connectivity Establishment), which helps ensure better connectivity in challenging network conditions. These updates ultimately contribute to a more robust and seamless real-time communication experience for users.
